newsitem.title: KENYA: Ugandan/Tanzanian capitals report torrential rains.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan/Tanzanian capitals report torrential rains.

text.p: The capitals of Uganda and Tanzania reported torrential rains overnight while the Kenyan capital remained overcast but saw no rain, weather officials in the region said on Tuesday.
"Kampala experienced an all-night long downpour which brought to an end a dry spell experienced in the capital since December," a weather official in Kampala said.
The Kampala rains lasted around eight hours and confounded weather officials who had predicted no rains in Kampala until the end of March and steady rains from mid-April.
The Tanzanian capital Dar es Salaam was flooded on Tuesday after it was drenched in overnight rain.

In Kenya, heavy rains were reported in Tigoni and Kiambu, on the outskirts of Nairobi, but the capital's commercial district still saw no rain. Weather officials said 66 millimetres of rain were recorded in the key coffee growing area of Embu.
Tanzania's weather office said the seasonal long rains had arrived, albeit too late to reverse severe drought damage in the agricultural sector, especially, in coffee, cotton and tea.

"Thunderstorms rolled over the coastal capital on Monday night continuing into the morning (on Tuesday), leaving drains overflowing, streets flooded and motor cars stalled," said a Dar es Salaam resident.
For most of Dar es Salaam's three million population, the rain was welcome news and a sign that two months of water shortage could finally be over.
Drought in East Africa had severely threatened food security and famine relief workers saw the rains as brightening prospects for the 1997/98 crop and easing fast-rising food prices.
